lessons.title: Yesterday I… (-ar verbs)

sentences.target: Ayer hablé con mi mamá por teléfono.
sentences.english: Yesterday I spoke with my mom on the phone.

sentences.target: Anoche trabajé hasta tarde.
sentences.english: Last night I worked until late.

sentences.target: Hace dos días compré un celular.
sentences.english: Two days ago I bought a cell phone.
sentences.spain: Hace dos días compré un móvil.

sentences.target: Ayer ustedes caminaron mucho.
sentences.english: Yesterday you all walked a lot.

sentences.target: Anteayer llamé a mi hermana.
sentences.english: The day before yesterday I called my sister.

sentences.target: La semana pasada esperé el autobús una hora.
sentences.english: Last week I waited for the bus for an hour.

fills.english: Yesterday I spoke with my sister.
Last night I waited for the bus.
What did you do yesterday?
Two days ago I called my friend.

dialogue.scene: A friend asks about your day

lines.english: What did you do yesterday?
I worked and bought a T-shirt.
And last night?

lessons.tip: Past of -ar verbs: drop -ar, add -é (I), -aste (you), -ó (he/she), -aron (they). The accent marks the past: hablo (I speak) vs habló (he spoke). Spain also says vosotros: hablasteis.

lessons.title: I ate, I lived (-er/-ir)

sentences.target: Escribí un mensaje y recibí un correo electrónico.

sentences.target: ¿Ustedes comieron en casa? ¿Qué comieron?
sentences.english: Did you all eat at home? What did you eat?

fills.english: Yesterday I ate chicken with rice.
My grandma lived in Madrid for ten years.
What did you eat last night?
I opened the door and went out.

lines.english: What did you eat last night?
I ate pizza. And you?

lines.target: Yo comí tacos y bebí una cerveza.
lines.english: I ate tacos and drank a beer.

lessons.tip: Past of -er/-ir: -í (I), -iste (you), -ió (he/she), -imos (we), -ieron (they). Same endings for both groups: comí, viví. Spain: comisteis (you all).

lessons.tip: Learn these past verbs as whole words: fui (I went/was), hice, tuve, estuve, vi. Ser and ir share the same past: fui = I went AND I was.

lessons.title: My weekend in chunks

example.english: It was great: I had a good time.

sentences.target: El sábado me desperté tarde y me quedé en casa.
sentences.english: On Saturday I woke up late and stayed home.

sentences.english: We went to the movies and watched a movie.

sentences.target: Comimos juntos y cenamos fuera.
sentences.english: We ate together and had dinner out.

sentences.target: Me divertí mucho; la pasé bien.
sentences.english: I had lots of fun; I had a good time.

Yesterday we went to the movies.
I had lots of fun. I had a good time.
I didn't go out; I stayed home.

lines.english: What did you do on Saturday?
I went to the movies with friends.
And how was it?

lessons.tip: Reflexive past just keeps 'me' in front: me levanté, me quedé, me divertí. Learn the weekend story as chunks. Spain says 'lo pasé bien'.

lessons.tip: Any past chat opens with ¿Qué hiciste? / ¿Cómo te fue? and answers in the pretérito. 'Lo hice' = I did it: lo sits before the verb. Spain: ¿Adónde fuisteis? for 'you all'.

lessons.title: Planning a trip

There are two of us: a double room.
I have a reservation under López.

Yes, under the name Smith.
Perfect. For how many nights?

lessons.tip: Quisiera reservar… and Tengo una reserva a nombre de… do 90% of hotel talk. Quisiera = polite 'I would like'. Spain says 'una reserva'.

lessons.tip: Airport words are mostly cognates. -ar verbs in the past change the spelling before -é: facturar → facturé, aterrizar → aterricé, despegar → despegué.

lessons.tip: Sightseeing nouns are mostly cognates or easy: la catedral, el castillo, la isla, la montaña. Learn each with its el/la: most -a words are la, -o words are el.

lessons.title: Appointments & lo/la

example.english: I want to cancel the appointment.
Can you give it to me, please?

sentences.target: Voy a confirmar la reunión.
sentences.english: I'm going to confirm the meeting.

sentences.target: ¿Estás disponible el viernes? Mi agenda está llena el lunes.
sentences.english: Are you available on Friday? My schedule is full on Monday.

sentences.target: Lo siento, voy a llegar tarde.
sentences.english: Sorry, I'm going to be late.

sentences.target: ¿Tienes el mapa? Sí, te lo mando ahora.
sentences.english: Do you have the map? Yes, I'll send it to you now.

sentences.target: ¿Ves a Ana? Sí, la veo mañana en la reunión.
sentences.english: Do you see Ana? Yes, I'll see her tomorrow at the meeting.

fills.english: Do you have the ticket? Yes, I have it.
I don't know.
It's the message: I'll send it to you now.
I'm seeing Ana tomorrow: I'll see her at the meeting.

No, I have another meeting. Thursday?
Thursday works. Do you confirm it?

lessons.tip: lo/la = it, and it goes before the verb: lo sé (I know it), la veo mañana (I see her tomorrow), te lo mando (I'll send it to you). Lo = masculine thing, la = feminine thing/person.

lessons.title: Staying healthy

lessons.tip: para + infinitive = in order to: para estar sano, para dormir mejor. Use it to give a reason for anything.

dialogue.scene: A friend wants to catch up

lines.english: When are you going to call me?
Later, I'm busy now.
What time later?

replyOptions: En un rato, a las seis.

lessons.tip: Time words carry the future, so the verb can stay simple: Mañana trabajo = I work tomorrow. Learn the time word first, the verb second.

lessons.tip: pienso + infinitive = I plan to; espero + infinitive = I hope to; me gustaría = I'd like to. Three chunks to talk about dreams without any new grammar.

lessons.tip: para = purpose or recipient (para ti, para mañana); por = through / by / duration (por aquí, por teléfono, por semana). Learn them as chunks first; the rule comes later.
